claim: The salivary gland tubes in Drosophila embryos form from a flat, nearly circular epithelial primordium called the salivary gland placode.
source: The symmetrical tubes of the embryonic salivary glands form from a flat, nearly circular epithelial primordium, the salivary gland placode (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The invagination point in the salivary gland placode is positioned asymmetrically in the dorsal-posterior corner rather than in the center.
source: Interestingly, the point of invagination from the circular placode primordium is not in the center of the placode, but in an asymmetric, eccentric position in the dorsal-posterior corner (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing the asymmetric positioning.

claim: Early apical constriction and cell wedging at the invagination pit initiates tissue bending in the salivary gland placode.
source: Using quantitative morphometric methods, we showed that the early apical constriction and associated cell wedging at the position of the invagination pit initiates the tissue bending (Booth et al., 2014; Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Isotropic constriction driven by apical-medial actomyosin is concentrated near the forming invagination pit.
source: Isotropic constriction driven by apical-medial actomyosin is concentrated near the forming invagination pit (Figure 1A' and A''), but at a distance to the pit a second cell behavior dominates cell intercalation.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 1A' and A''.

claim: Cell intercalation driven by polarised junctional actomyosin helps elongate the tissue radially toward the invagination pit and contract it circumferentially.
source: Driven by a polarised junctional accumulation of actomyosin, cell intercalation events such as T1 exchanges and rosette formation and resolution help to elongate the tissue radially toward the invagination pit and contract it circumferentially, via circumferential neighbor gains (Figure 1A'; Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 1A' and a citation.

claim: Cells near the invagination pit continuously constrict until internalized.
source: Note that cells near the pit continuously constrict until internalized (pink shaded box), whereas cells far from the pit do not constrict significantly until t=20 min whilst moving closer to the pit (gray shaded box), but once they are in close proximity to the pit they also constrict until internalized (blue shaded box).
evidence: This is stated in the text describing Figure 1E and supported by the data shown in the figure.

claim: Cells far from the pit do not constrict significantly until t=20 min while moving closer to the pit.
source: Note that cells near the pit continuously constrict until internalized (pink shaded box), whereas cells far from the pit do not constrict significantly until t=20 min whilst moving closer to the pit (gray shaded box), but once they are in close proximity to the pit they also constrict until internalized (blue shaded box).
evidence: This is stated in the text describing Figure 1E and supported by the data shown in the figure.

claim: Once cells far from the pit are in close proximity to the pit, they also constrict until internalized.
source: Note that cells near the pit continuously constrict until internalized (pink shaded box), whereas cells far from the pit do not constrict significantly until t=20 min whilst moving closer to the pit (gray shaded box), but once they are in close proximity to the pit they also constrict until internalized (blue shaded box).
evidence: This is stated in the text describing Figure 1E and supported by the data shown in the figure.

claim: Apical constriction is always strongest near the invagination pit at any moment in time.
source: We found that apical constriction is always strongest near the invagination pit at any moment in time.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: As coronae of cells approach the region near the pit, they switch behavior from predominantly intercalating to predominantly apically constricting/wedging.
source: As more and more coronae of cells approach the region near the pit, they switch behavior from predominantly intercalating to predominantly apically constricting/wedging.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: The continued near-pit constriction is driven by apical-medial myosin, whose peak intensity and peak pulsatile strength is tracked in a fixed position close to the pit over time.
source: The continued near-pit constriction is driven by apical-medial myosin, whose peak intensity and peak pulsatile strength is tracked in a fixed position close to the pit over time.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: Hkb and Fkh expression levels pre-pattern where initial constriction is occurring.
source: Using live-imaging of endogenous fluorescently tagged versions of Hkb and Fkh, we show that their expression levels pre-pattern where initial constriction is occurring.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: Hkb and Fkh are upstream of a dynamic patterning of the GPCR ligand Fog.
source: Both are upstream of a dynamic patterning of the GPCR ligand Fog, that in turn activates apical-medial myosin.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: Fog activates apical-medial myosin.
source: Both are upstream of a dynamic patterning of the GPCR ligand Fog, that in turn activates apical-medial myosin.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: Loss of correct pre-patterning in hkb−/− mutants leads to loss of symmetrical final organ shape with a narrow lumen.
source: Loss of the correct pre-patterning, such as in hkb−/− mutants or when Fog is overexpressed, leads to loss of the symmetrical final organ shape with a narrow lumen and instead gives rise to expanded and sack-like glands with widened lumena.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: Overexpression of Fog leads to loss of symmetrical final organ shape with a narrow lumen and gives rise to expanded and sack-like glands with widened lumena.
source: Loss of the correct pre-patterning, such as in hkb−/− mutants or when Fog is overexpressed, leads to loss of the symmetrical final organ shape with a narrow lumen and instead gives rise to expanded and sack-like glands with widened lumena.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: Cells near the pit at t=0 min displayed isotropic constriction and were internalized by about t=+20 min.
source: Cells positioned near the pit at t=0 min (Figure 1B, pink) constricted their apices isotropically and rapidly and were internalized by about t=+ 20 min (Figure 1B and C and dashed curve in Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1B, C, and E.

claim: Cells positioned far from the pit at t=0 min began constricting as they moved into a position closer to the invagination point.
source: Cells positioned far from the pit at t=0 min (Figure 1B, gray) and moving into a position closer to the invagination point began constricting (Figure 1B and D and solid curve in Figure 1E; Figure 1—video 1), suggesting that cells changed their behavior depending on where they were positioned in the placode with respect to the invagination point.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1B, D, and E.

claim: Cells change their behavior depending on where they are positioned in the placode with respect to the invagination point.
source: Cells positioned far from the pit at t=0 min (Figure 1B, gray) and moving into a position closer to the invagination point began constricting (Figure 1B and D and solid curve in Figure 1E; Figure 1—video 1), suggesting that cells changed their behavior depending on where they were positioned in the placode with respect to the invagination point.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a suggestion based on the data shown in figures.

claim: Cells near the pit showed strong accumulation of apical-medial myosin at t=0 min.
source: cells near the future invagination point at t=0 min showed strong accumulation of apical-medial myosin (Figure 2A, A'' and C; see also Figure 2—video 1)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A, A'', and C.

claim: Cells far from the pit and close to the anterior placode boundary showed mainly junctional myosin II accumulation at t=0 min.
source: whereas cells far from the pit and close to the anterior placode boundary (Figure 2A and A') showed mainly junctional myosin II accumulation.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A and A'.

claim: At t=30 min, cells located right next to the invagination pit continued to display strong apical-medial myosin accumulation.
source: At t=30 min, the cells now located right next to the invagination pit continued to display strong apical-medial myosin accumulation (Figure 2B and B'')
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B and B''.

claim: Cells initially far from the pit but now in closer proximity to the pit at t=30 min started to display apical-medial actomyosin.
source: but in addition cells that were initially 'far from the pit,' but were now in a closer proximity to the pit though still near the anterior boundary, now also started to display apical-medial actomyosin (Figure 2B and B').
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B and B'.

claim: Being moved into a position near the invagination pit determines levels of apical-medial myosin accumulation.
source: Thus, being moved into a position near the invagination pit appeared to determine levels of apical-medial myosin accumulation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations described.

claim: The peak of apical-medial myosin fluorescence intensity tracked in a near-fixed position to the edge of the pit over time.
source: Looking placode-wide over the whole time period analyzed, the peak of the apical-medial myosin fluorescence intensity tracked in a near-fixed position to the edge of the pit over time (Figure 2D, white dotted line).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2D.

claim: The location of the highest medial myosin intensity was where cells showed the shortest cycle lengths of medial myosin II fluctuations.
source: The location of the highest medial myosin intensity was also where cells showed the shortest cycle lengths of medial myosin II fluctuations (Figure 2E, white dotted line).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2E.

claim: Cells near the pit at t=0 min showed an overall shorter myosin II cycle length compared to cells located far from the pit.
source: Interestingly, cells near the pit at t=0 min showed an overall shorter myosin II cycle length (the time period elapsed between two peaks of highest myosin II intensity during the oscillation, see schematic in Figure 2E) compared to cells located far from the pit (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2F.

claim: Longer myosin II cycle length correlates with unproductive myosin cycles.
source: As longer cycle length correlates with unproductive myosin cycles (Booth et al., 2014), this was in line with cells further away from the pit showing less apical constriction.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Cells further away from the pit show less apical constriction.
source: As longer cycle length correlates with unproductive myosin cycles (Booth et al., 2014), this was in line with cells further away from the pit showing less apical constriction.
evidence: This is stated in the text as an inference based on the correlation with cycle length.

claim: Myosin strength across the placode at t=0 min was much higher in cells near the invagination point with a gradual decrease toward the placode boundary.
source: This myosin strength across the placode at t=0 min was much higher in cells near the invagination point when plotted against the distance to the pit, with a gradual decrease in myosin strength toward the placode boundary (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2G.

claim: Cells originally far from the pit at t=0 min increased their myosin strength over time whilst moving into a position closer to the pit.
source: However, cells originally far from the pit at t=0 min increased their myosin strength over time (and concomitantly decreased their cycle length; see Figure 2—figure supplement 1) whilst moving into a position closer to the pit, so that by t=55 min their myosin strength had increased to levels previously shown by cells near the pit at t=0 min (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: By t=55 min, cells originally far from the pit had myosin strength levels similar to cells near the pit at t=0 min.
source: However, cells originally far from the pit at t=0 min increased their myosin strength over time (and concomitantly decreased their cycle length; see Figure 2—figure supplement 1) whilst moving into a position closer to the pit, so that by t=55 min their myosin strength had increased to levels previously shown by cells near the pit at t=0 min (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2H.

claim: hkb−/− mutants show a delayed central invagination pit compared to the eccentric pit observed in wild-type placodes.
source: Thus, hkb−/− mutants show a delayed central invagination pit compared to the eccentric pit observed in wild-type placodes (Figure 3(I)1').
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3I1'.

claim: In hkb−/− mutant placodes, cells began to constrict in an aberrant central position from about t=+20–30 min.
source: In contrast, in hkb−/− mutant placodes cells began to constrict in an aberrant central position from about t=+20–30 min (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3G and H.

claim: The rate of constriction of central cells in hkb−/− mutants was very similar to that of cells located at a distance to the pit in the wild-type.
source: In fact, the rate of the constriction of the central cells in hkb−/− mutants was very similar to that of the cells located at a distance to the pit in the wild-type (compare blue dashed and magenta solid curves), suggesting that the central cells in hkb−/− mutants continue to behave identical to the wild-type cells occupying the same position.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by comparison of curves in Figure 3J.

claim: Central cells in hkb−/− mutants continue to behave identically to wild-type cells occupying the same position.
source: In fact, the rate of the constriction of the central cells in hkb−/− mutants was very similar to that of the cells located at a distance to the pit in the wild-type (compare blue dashed and magenta solid curves), suggesting that the central cells in hkb−/− mutants continue to behave identical to the wild-type cells occupying the same position.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the similarity in constriction rates.

claim: Cells far from the central pit in hkb−/− mutants showed a slight apical area expansion up to t=+20 min followed by a slight constriction, but did not invaginate over the time interval shown.
source: Cells far from the central pit in hkb−/− mutants showed a slight apical area expansion up to t=+20 min followed by a slight constriction, but did not invaginate over the time interval shown in the plots.
evidence: This is stated in the text referring to plots in Figure 3J.

claim: hkb−/− mutant placodes showed no accumulation of apical-medial actomyosin at the eccentric position where a pit forms in the wild-type.
source: In agreement with the delayed central constriction of cells in hkb−/− mutant placodes, we found no accumulation of apical-medial actomyosin at the eccentric position where a pit forms in the wild-type (compare Figure 3E and K to Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by comparison of figures.

claim: At t~+40 min, a central group of cells in hkb−/− mutant placodes displayed increased accumulation of apical-medial myosin II.
source: Instead, only at t~+40 min did a central group of cells in hkb−/− mutant placodes display increased accumulation of apical-medial myosin II (Figure 3K), inducing a shallow tissue bending in this region at this point (see also Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3K and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In wild-type placodes, cells near the eccentric invagination pit constricted isotropically, with near equal change in strain at the tissue and cell shape level, and very little intercalation strain.
source: In wild-type placodes, cells that were located near the eccentric invagination pit (Figure 4A; with the 'near' position defined at t=0 min; see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1) constricted isotropically, with near equal change in strain at the tissue and cell shape level, and very little intercalation strain (Figure 4A' and A'', solid curves).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4A, A', and A''.

claim: In wild-type placodes, cells near the pit could only be tracked up to t=20 min as they had all invaginated by this point.
source: These cells in wild-type placodes could only be tracked up to t=20 min as at this point they had all invaginated into the embryo to form the initial part of the tube.
evidence: This is stated in the text as an observation from the tracking analysis.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, cells near the forming central pit showed a much reduced tissue and cell shape strain rate, with near identical radial and circumferential contributions.
source: In contrast, in the hkb−/− mutants, cells near the forming central pit (Figure 4A; defined to be in a 'near' position at t=0 min) showed a much reduced tissue and cell shape strain rate, with near identical radial and circumferential contributions, and constriction only commenced at about half the rate of the wild-type placodes from t=+20 min onwards (Figure 4A' and A'', dashed curves; see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4A, A', and A''.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, constriction of cells near the central pit only commenced at about half the rate of wild-type placodes from t=+20 min onwards.
source: In contrast, in the hkb−/− mutants, cells near the forming central pit (Figure 4A; defined to be in a 'near' position at t=0 min) showed a much reduced tissue and cell shape strain rate, with near identical radial and circumferential contributions, and constriction only commenced at about half the rate of the wild-type placodes from t=+20 min onwards (Figure 4A' and A'', dashed curves; see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4A, A', and A''.

claim: In wild-type placodes, cells far from the eccentric pit showed cell intercalations leading to circumferential convergence and radial extension of the tissue over the first approximately 20 min after invagination commenced.
source: In wild-type placodes, cells far from the eccentric pit (Figure 4B; defined to be 'far' at t=0 min), showed cell intercalations leading to circumferential convergence and radial extension of the tissue over the first approximately 20 min after invagination commenced, as we also reported previously (Figure 4B' and B'', solid curves; tissue and intercalation strain rate showing expansion radially and contraction circumferentially; Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B, B', and B'' and a citation.

claim: In wild-type placodes, cells far from the pit switched behavior to apical contraction after t=+20 min once they were located closer to the pit position.
source: Interestingly, we then observed a clear switch in cell behavior of these cells to a second phase after t=+20 min. Once these cells were located closer to the pit position, they now also displayed apical contraction (beyond t=+20 min; Figure 4B' and B'', solid green curves).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B' and B''.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, for cells at the placode periphery far from the central constriction, the tissue expanded slightly in both radial and circumferential direction.
source: In the hkb−/− mutants, for cells at the placode periphery and hence far from the central constriction (Figure 4B), the tissue expanded slightly in both radial and circumferential direction (Figure 4B' and B'', dashed gray curves)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B, B', and B''.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, cells at the placode periphery showed cell shapes narrowing radially and extending circumferentially.
source: In the hkb−/− mutants, for cells at the placode periphery and hence far from the central constriction (Figure 4B), the tissue expanded slightly in both radial and circumferential direction (Figure 4B' and B'', dashed gray curves), with cell shapes narrowing radially (dashed green curve in Figure 4B') and extending circumferentially (dashed green curve in Figure 4B'').
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B' and B''.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, cells at the placode periphery showed a similar rate of intercalation as cells far from the pit in wild-type placodes, with some radial elongation and circumferential contraction.
source: We could observe a similar rate of intercalation in these cells as in cells far from the pit in wild-type placodes, with some radial elongation and circumferential contraction (dashed orange curves in Figure 4B' and B'').
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B' and B''.

claim: In wild-type placodes, circumferential neighbor gains dominate over radial neighbor gains throughout.
source: In wild-type placodes, circumferential neighbor gains outweigh radial ones by a large margin throughout (Figure 4D, dashed curves), leading to a steady increase in cumulative productive neighbor gains for cells across the placode (Figure 4E, yellow curves).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4D and E.

claim: In hkb−/− mutant embryos, circumferential and radial neighbor gains across the placode were overall much reduced in number and occurred with equal frequency.
source: In contrast, in hkb−/− mutant embryos circumferential and radial neighbor gains across the placode were overall much reduced in number and occurred with equal frequency (Figure 4D, solid curves).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4D.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, cells near the delayed central pit showed no productive neighbor gains.
source: Furthermore, cells near the delayed central pit in hkb−/− mutants showed no productive neighbor gains (defined as the difference between circumferential and radial neighbor gains, corrected for the proportion of interfaces that could successfully be tracked; Figure 4E, purple dashed curve)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4E.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, cells at the periphery away from the central pit showed productive neighbor gains.
source: whereas cells at the periphery away from the central pit showed productive neighbor gains (Figure 4E, solid purple curve).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4E.

claim: In control placodes, junctional myosin is clearly enriched in circumferential junctions up to the point of most secretory cells having internalized by t=+40 min.
source: Whereas in control placodes junctional myosin is clearly enriched in circumferential junctions by both measures, up to the point of most secretory cells having internalized by t=+40 min (Figure 4F and G; dashed green curve vs. dashed purple curve)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4F and G.

claim: In hkb−/− mutant placodes, myosin unipolarity and bipolarity are strongly reduced.
source: in hkb−/− mutant placodes myosin unipolarity and bipolarity are strongly reduced, even though some bipolarity remained (Figure 4F and G, solid curves).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4F and G.

claim: In wild-type placodes, cells far from the pit are initially elongated circumferentially at t<+20 min while early intercalation events are initiated by circumferential junctional myosin.
source: We also analyzed cell elongation in cells far from the pit, with cells in wild-type placodes being initially elongated circumferentially at t<+20 min, while early intercalation events are initiated by circumferential junctional myosin (Figure 4H, gray curve; Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4H and a citation.

claim: In wild-type placodes, cells far from the pit become increasingly elongated radially as they move into a position nearer to the pit and are being actively funneled toward the pit.
source: These cells then became increasingly elongated radially as they moved into a position nearer to the pit and were being actively funneled toward the pit.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the behavior of cells in wild-type placodes.

claim: In hkb−/− mutant embryos, cells far from the pit at the periphery of the placode very quickly became circumferentially elongated and remained so throughout the time period analyzed.
source: In hkb−/− mutant embryos, cells far from the pit at the periphery of the placode very quickly became circumferentially elongated and remained so throughout the time period analyzed.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the behavior of cells in hkb−/− mutant embryos.

claim: In cells far from the central pit in hkb−/− mutants, groups of cells undergo intercalations with individual cells making circumferential neighbor gains and elongating, whilst the overall shape of the local group of cells undergoing the intercalation event was not changing.
source: In cells far from the central pit in hkb−/− mutants, we could observe groups of cells clearly undergoing intercalations (Figure 4I and J) with individual cells making circumferential neighbor gains and elongating (cells 1 and 2 in Figure 4K), whilst the overall shape of the local group of cells undergoing the intercalation event was not changing (Figure 4L).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4I, J, K, and L.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, intercalations lacked several key signatures of wild-type intercalations and overall did not lead to convergence and extension of the tissue toward the misplaced pit.
source: Thus, although cells far from the aberrant central pit in hkb−/− mutants still intercalated and gained circumferential neighbors, this behavior lacked several key signatures of wild-type intercalations, and overall in the hkb−/− mutants intercalations did not lead to convergence and extension of the tissue toward the misplaced pit.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations described.

claim: In the absence of Hkb, the initial radial patterning of cell behaviors across the placode is highly aberrant.
source: These analyses show that in the absence of Hkb, the initial radial patterning of cell behaviors across the placode is highly aberrant.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the analyses presented.

claim: Cells located at the position corresponding to where the eccentric pit would be located in the wild-type clearly failed to constrict apically in hkb−/− mutants.
source: Cells located at the position corresponding to where the eccentric pit would be located in the wild-type clearly failed to constrict apically, suggesting that Hkb could be involved in the specification of this pit behavior observed in wild-type.
evidence: This is stated in the text as an observation from the analyses.

claim: Hkb could be involved in the specification of the pit behavior observed in wild-type.
source: Cells located at the position corresponding to where the eccentric pit would be located in the wild-type clearly failed to constrict apically, suggesting that Hkb could be involved in the specification of this pit behavior observed in wild-type.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the observation that cells fail to constrict in hkb−/− mutants.

claim: Venus-Hkb was detected at high levels concentrated in the dorsal-posterior region of the just forming placode at t=–30 min prior to the first tissue bending.
source: Using this in vivo reporter, we detected Venus-Hkb at high levels concentrated in the dorsal-posterior region of the just forming placode, in the area where the invagination pit will form, already at t=–30 min prior to the first tissue bending (Figure 5A, A', D and M and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,B'' ), and even as early as t=–63 min prior to invagination (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A, A', D, M and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Venus-Hkb was detected as early as t=–63 min prior to invagination.
source: Using this in vivo reporter, we detected Venus-Hkb at high levels concentrated in the dorsal-posterior region of the just forming placode, in the area where the invagination pit will form, already at t=–30 min prior to the first tissue bending (Figure 5A, A', D and M and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,B'' ), and even as early as t=–63 min prior to invagination (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Venus-Hkb expression expanded more broadly and anteriorly across the whole placode over time.
source: The expression then expanded more broadly and anteriorly across the whole placode over time (Figure 5B–C', E, F and M and Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B–C', E, F, M and Figure 5—video 1.

claim: At t=0 min, Venus-Hkb was found across the placode, with elevated levels still at the invagination pit position, and a second increase toward the anterior.
source: At the moment of first tissue bending (t=0 min) Venus-Hkb was found across the placode, with elevated levels still at the invagination pit position, and a second increase toward the anterior.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the pattern at t=0 min.

claim: At late stages (t>>0 min), Venus-Hkb levels close to the invagination point were lower than further anterior.
source: At late stages (t>>0 min) Venus-Hkb levels close to the invagination point were lower than further anterior (Figure 5M).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5M.

claim: As early as 1 hr before tissue bending, Fkh is already expressed at the posterior corner.
source: Stills of a time-lapse movie of embryos with Fkh tagged by GFP under endogenous expression control, at t=–60 min, +0 min and +30 min show that as early as 1 hr before tissue bending, Fkh is already expressed at the posterior corner.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 5G–L and supported by the images.

claim: Fkh-GFP was visible in the cells near the future invagination pit already at t=–60 min prior to tissue bending.
source: Already at t=–60 min prior to tissue bending, Fkh-GFP was visible in the cells near the future invagination pit (Figure 5G, G', J and N and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–C'')
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5G, G', J, N and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Fkh-GFP expression spread anteriorly and ventrally across the whole placode from the future invagination pit.
source: from where it spread anteriorly and ventrally across the whole placode (Figure 5—video 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—video 2.

claim: At t=0 min, Fkh-GFP was detected in all cells of the placode, with levels still highest near the pit and decreasing toward the anterior edge of the placode.
source: At t=0 min, Fkh-GFP was already detected in all cells of the placode, though with levels still highest near the pit and decreasing toward the anterior edge of the placode (Figure 5H, H', K and N).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5H, H', K, and N.

claim: At t=+30 min and beyond, levels of Fkh-GFP were more uniform across the placode.
source: At t=+30 min and beyond, levels of Fkh-GFP were more uniform across the placode (Figure 5I, I', L, N).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5I, I', L, and N.

claim: Both Hkb and Fkh transcription factors showed a clear temporally and spatially graded pattern of expression within the early placode that developed dynamically.
source: Thus, both Hkb and Fkh transcription factors showed a clear temporally and spatially graded pattern of expression within the early placode that developed dynamically.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations of Venus-Hkb and Fkh-GFP expression.

claim: Changes in Hkb and Fkh expression were especially pronounced at the dorsal-posterior corner, with highest levels here already an hour before tissue bending commenced.
source: Changes were especially pronounced at the dorsal-posterior corner, with highest levels here already an hour before tissue bending commenced.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations of Venus-Hkb and Fkh-GFP expression.

claim: Combined Hkb and Fkh action could define the future position of the invagination pit.
source: Combined Hkb and Fkh action could thereby define the future position of the invagination pit.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the expression patterns observed.

claim: Venus-Hkb intensity levels peaked in cells located at the site of the forming eccentric invagination pit at about t ~ –30 min.
source: Venus-Hkb intensity levels peaked in cells located at the site of the forming eccentric invagination pit at about t ~ –30 min (Figure 5O)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5O.

claim: An appearance of smaller apical areas at the site of the forming eccentric invagination pit followed the peak of Venus-Hkb intensity by about 30–40 min.
source: with an appearance of smaller apical areas in this position following on about 30–40 min later (Figure 5O').
